title: Writing a Grocery List
description: Write down household foods before heading to the store.
cardDescription: Write down household foods before heading to the store.
focus: The setting is writing a Grocery List. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Material used for writing or wrapping
Writing tool with a graphite core
Food baked from flour and dough
Oval food with a shell, white, and yolk
Written order to a bank to pay money
One thing on a shopping list
Small soft cushion placed under something

answerNotes.LIST: A list records items in order. Checking off a purchased item is different from changing the price or quantity of it.
answerNotes.GROCERY: Grocery describes food and household shopping. A list records intended purchases; the bags contain what was actually bought.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.PENCIL: The writing core of a modern pencil is graphite, not metallic lead. Lead remains a traditional everyday name for it.
answerNotes.MILK: Milk is a dairy liquid used in drinks and batters. Cream is the richer portion, with a higher fat content.
answerNotes.BREAD: Bread may be a whole loaf or pieces cut from it. A loaf is counted as a whole, while a slice is one flat portion.
answerNotes.EGG: A hen's egg has a shell, white, and yolk. Recipes sometimes use only one inner part rather than the whole egg.
answerNotes.ITEM: An item is one entry or object in a group. The same list can include individual foods, packages, and other household supplies.
answerNotes.NOTE: A note is a short written message. It can be a reminder, a greeting, or a brief explanation attached to an object.

answerNotes.ENVELOPE: An envelope encloses a letter. The destination goes on its front; the message stays inside.
answerNotes.STAMP: Stamp can mean a postage label or a tool that leaves an ink impression. A mailed letter and a craft project use different senses.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign can be a public notice or the action of writing a name. Check whether the clue describes an object or asks for a verb.
answerNotes.ADDRESS: An address tells where mail should go. The recipient's name identifies the person, while the street, city, and postal code locate the destination.
answerNotes.PEN: A pen writes with ink. A pencil uses graphite, which can usually be removed with an eraser.

answerNotes.CALENDAR: A calendar organizes dates into weeks and months. Months vary in length, so a month is not exactly four weeks.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
answerNotes.PAGE: A page is one side of a book's paper. A single physical leaf normally has two pages, front and back.
answerNotes.CIRCLE: A circle is a round line or shape. In a marble game, a drawn circle can mark the playing area.
answerNotes.NOTE: A note is a short written message. It can be a reminder, a greeting, or a brief explanation attached to an object.
answerNotes.NUMBER: A number can count an amount or identify something. A telephone number identifies a connection rather than measuring its size.

answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.STAMP: Stamp can mean a postage label or a tool that leaves an ink impression. A mailed letter and a craft project use different senses.
answerNotes.ENVELOPE: An envelope encloses a letter. The destination goes on its front; the message stays inside.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.ADDRESS: An address tells where mail should go. The recipient's name identifies the person, while the street, city, and postal code locate the destination.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.

answerNotes.FILE: File can mean an organized collection or the act of putting papers away. In a desk scene, it is not the rough metal tool used in a workshop.
answerNotes.FOLDER: A folder groups loose papers without binding them into a book. A label on its tab helps the stored pages be found again.
answerNotes.DRAWER: A drawer slides in and out of furniture. Its front may have a handle, while dividers separate the contents inside.
answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.RECEIPT: A receipt records a completed payment. A bill asks for payment, so the two papers serve different purposes.
